title: The Star-Eater
author: Radiant Ilsara sari-Qadrun
pages: In the first days Azhir walked the sky and Nahire walked beside him, the Dawn, the gentle twin. Where he was law she was mercy. Every morning she went before him and opened the doors of the east.
But at the world's edge, where the stars run out, lay a thing of black wings and hunger. It envied her light. One evening as she lingered at the rim of the sky, it rose and swallowed her whole.
Azhir burned with grief, and the sands remember his tears as glass. Since that day the dawn is grey and brief, and night has teeth. The Star-Eater sleeps in the dark beyond the stars, fat with her.
Know this, faithful: what is swallowed is not destroyed. Slay the Star-Eater and Nahire will rise from its body and the twin dawn will return. This is the hope of the Unfading, and it is holy.
Therefore the Burning Mirror keeps its swords bright. Therefore we fast on Nahire's Mourning and veil our mirrors. Therefore we do not sit in darkness and call it wisdom, as the star-watchers do.
